title: Crypto Telemetry & Incident Key Forensics Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines telemetry signals, SIEM export schema mappings, and step-by-step forensic procedures to gather, preserve, and analyze cryptographic evidence after an incident that may involve keys (KMS/HSM/BYOK) or encryption-at-rest. It is intended for incident response (IR), security engineers, platform SREs, and compliance auditors.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers hosted KMS calls, on-prem HSM events, and customer BYOK key usage visible to Redwood control plane.
- Assumes RBAC v2 is the authoritative source of actor roles and privileges for all services.
- Focuses on telemetry required to: reconstruct timeline, prove key provenance/usage, detect privilege misuse, and produce SIEM-friendly artifacts for retention and e-discovery.
- Not a key-rotation procedure; cross-references rotation playbooks for remediation actions.

High-level objectives:
1) Define a minimal, consistent audit schema that spans KMS API, HSM audit streams, RBAC events, and platform traces.
2) Provide automated evidence collection steps (scripts/playbooks) that package logs, config snapshots, and signed manifests for legal/compliance.
3) Detail forensic triage runbook: verify compromise, scope blast radius, preserve key material state (no destructive ops), and coordinate with customers for BYOK keys.

RBAC v2 integration (why it matters):
- RBAC v2 gives us role tiers (platform-admin, sec-operator, infra-deployer, customer-admin, service-account) and scope (global, org, project, resource).
- For every cryptographic operation in the audit stream we must associate: actor_id, actor_role (from RBAC v2 effective role), actor_scope, and policy_snapshot_id.
- Actionable enforcement: when an event shows a sensitive op (eg. key_export, key_unwrap, hsm-slot-manipulate), IR tooling should check the RBAC decision log for the decision hash and include it in the evidence bundle.

Core audit log schema (single canonical flat schema for SIEM export):
- event_time: ISO8601 UTC timestamp
- receipt_time: ingestion timestamp of the audit collector
- tenant_id: tenant or customer id
- resource_type: KMS_KEY | HSM_MODULE | SECRET_STORE | VM_DISK
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier (kms://region/tenant/key/alias)
- operation: CREATE | READ | UPDATE | DELETE | ENCRYPT | DECRYPT | SIGN | VERIFY | EXPORT | ROTATE | KEY_POLICY_CHANGE | HSM_SLOT_ACCESS
- key_id: key identifier (empty for non-key resource events)
- key_version: version string or incremental id
- hsm_slot: for HSM events; slot identifier or NULL
- actor_id: principal id (user/service)
- actor_display_name: friendly name if available
- actor_role: effective RBAC v2 role string
- actor_scope: effective scope id or path
- auth_mechanism: oauth | service_token | mTLS | hsm-cert
- outcome: SUCCESS | FAILURE | DENIED | PARTIAL
- error_code: internal code or null
- request_id: unique request id from service gateway
- correlation_id: trace-friendly id (for cross-service correlation)
- trace_id: distributed trace id if present
- request_payload_hash: sha256 of request body (redacts secrets)
- response_payload_hash: sha256 (redacts secrets)
- call_latency_ms: observed latency in ms
- client_ip: best-effort source IP (redact per policy)
- region: cloud region or datacenter id
- retention_tier: HOT | WARM | COLD (computed)
- evidence_tag: label(s) applied by automation (eg. "legal_hold_2026-03")
- raw_log_link: pointer to raw log bundle in evidence storage
- policy_snapshot_id: id of the RBAC/policy state at time of event
- notes: free-form for analyst annotations

SIEM export considerations:
- Normalize timestamps to UTC and include both event_time and receipt_time for ingestion lag analysis.
- Export via secure forwarder with mutual TLS and attestation. Use JSON-lines compressed per hour.
- Include request_id and correlation_id to enable deterministic joins between KMS, API gateway, RBAC decision logs, and app traces.
- Mask/pseudonymize PII and key material: never export plaintext key material or unredacted secrets. Include only fingerprints/hashes for verification.
- Retention tiers: keep HOT (30d), WARM (365d), COLD (7y) for events flagged by evidence_tag or legal_hold.

Automated evidence packaging (evidence automation flow):
1) Trigger: IR runbook stage "preserve" is executed (manual or automated on detection rule).
2) Collector agents (infra sidecar + HSM audit forwarder) snapshot:
   - Rolling KMS audit logs for +/- 24h around event_time
   - HSM audit tape (slot logs, operator sessions) for relevant HSM module(s)
   - RBAC decision log for queries referencing actor_id and resource_id
   - Model of key metadata: creation_time, origin (generated|imported), BYOK_customer_id, wrap_algorithm, policy_snapshot_id, rotation_history
   - Configuration snapshots: broker bindings, network ACLs, IAM policy exports (policy_snapshot_id), list of active service tokens with last_used timestamps
3) Evidence bundling: package artifacts into a signed archive with a manifest.json (manifest lists artifact names, sha256, collector_id, timestamp, and a signature using an internal forensics key).
4) Ingest into evidence-store: write to WORM storage with immutability flag and assign evidence_id. Update case ticket (JIRA/IR) with evidence_id and raw_log_link pointers.
5) SIEM index: create a case-scoped index or tag the events with evidence_id and legal_hold flag. Ensure index is snapshotted to cold-tier immutable backup.

Forensics runbook (triage -> full investigation):
Phase 0: Prepare (pre-incident)
- Confirm telemetry retention and collector health daily.
- Ensure HSM audit forwarding is on and that module certificates are rotated per key schedule.
- Maintain a mapping of BYOK customer ids to escrow/consent artifacts.
- Ensure RBAC policy versioning (policy_snapshot_id) is recorded at every policy change.

Phase 1: Initial triage (first 2 hours)
1) Validate alert: capture alert metadata (alert_id, detector_rule, initial_event_time).
2) Query SIEM for related events by correlation_id, request_id, actor_id, key_id +/- 24h.
3) If key operation is sensitive (EXPORT or UNWRAP), immediately take preservation actions (lock key for rotation-only or freeze access) — consult legal before destructive ops.
4) Notify oncall KMS lead + security manager + legal.

Phase 2: Contain & preserve (2-24 hours)
- Run automated evidence packaging flow.
- Export RBAC decision log for actor and policy_snapshot at event_time.
- Snapshot HSM operator session logs; mark HSM module as under investigation in asset inventory.
- Capture full config of the KMS key: origin, wrapping key id, allowed_encryption_contexts, rotation schedule, last_rotation_time, imported_by (if BYOK), import_evidence_id.
- For BYOK: reach out to customer contact per BYOK-process and request any logs or attestations in parallel (follow the BYOK SLA for disclosure).

Phase 3: Deep analysis (24h-14d)
- Correlate RBAC grants changes with timeline. Did any role escalate shortly before the operation?
- Reconstruct the distributed trace across services using trace_id and correlation_id.
- Look for anomalous non-replayable sequences: repeated key_unwrap attempts, sudden increases in decrypt operations, or unusual client_ip patterns.
- If HSM shows physical slot tampering or operator consoles show direct slot access, escalate to platform SRE and CISO.

Preservation / legal hold guidance:
- Evidence-bundles marked for legal_hold must move to immutable cold-tier and be retained for a minimum of 7 years or per legal directive.
- Document chain-of-custody in manifest and append analyst_signoff entries for every access to the bundle.
- Avoid any operation that rotates or destroys key material until legal/forensics signoff unless immediate mitigation (eg. revocation) is necessary to stop ongoing data exfiltration. Document rationale.

Emergency key operations (when necessary):
- Emergency revoke (soft): disable the key (deny new encrypt/decrypt ops) with operational timestamp and an evidence snapshot. This preserves key material while stopping new usage.
- Emergency rotate (hard): only with authorization from security manager + legal; rotation must be done with a recorded job that emits a rotation_job_id and includes pre/post-manifest snapshots.
- Export policy: key exports from HSMs are forbidden except under documented exception and must be done via a sealed ceremony logged by at least 2 operators; the export event must include operator_ids, card/usb serials, and HSM attestation log.

Sample SIEM queries (examples to run in Splunk / KQL):
- Splunk: index=kms_events (key_id=K-12345) | where operation="EXPORT" OR operation="UNWRAP" | stats count by actor_id, actor_role, region, outcome
- KQL (Elastic): event.dataset:kms and key_id:"K-12345" and (operation:EXPORT or operation:UNWRAP) | sort by @timestamp desc | limit 500
- Cross-index join pattern: join on correlation_id between api-gateway logs and kms_events to reconstruct request path.

Evidence manifest example (manifest fields to include in bundle):
- evidence_id: unique id
- generated_by: collector host id
- generated_at: ISO timestamp
- included_artifacts: list of filenames
- artifact_hashes: map file->sha256 (include as separate flat list entries in manifest)
- signed_by: collector-signing-key-id
- rbacsnapshot_id: policy_snapshot_id used to resolve roles
- notes: free text

Operational telemetry checklist (pre-incident):
- KMS audit forwarding enabled and validated end-to-end every 24 hours.
- HSM audit stream healthchecks (log rotation, time sync) configured.
- RBAC policy snapshot automation in place for every policy change.
- Evidence-store immutability and access control reviewed quarterly.
- Emergency contact list for BYOK customers reviewed monthly.

Appendix A — Glossary (short):
- BYOK: Bring Your Own Key (customer imports key into Redwood-managed KMS or a wrapped BYOK pattern)
- HSM slot: physical/virtual key slot on HSM where key material is resident
- RBAC v2: our role-based access control system with versioned policies and decision logs
- Evidence bundle: signed archive of logs/config used for legal/compliance

Appendix B — Quick templates
- IR slack alert template (short):
  "Incident: possible key compromise; evidence_id: {{evidence_id}}; initial_event_time: {{t}}; actor_id: {{actor}}; key_id: {{key}}; next steps: preserve snapshot and notify legal"

- Email to BYOK customer (sensitive):
  "Subject: Redwood incident notification — request for BYOK context
   Hi <CustomerSec>,
   We detected an unusual KMS operation involving an imported key (key alias {{key}}) on {{t}}. We have preserved audit logs and would like any additional telemetry you can share (key import receipt, operator ids, client IPs) under our BYOK disclosure process. Please reply with the designated contact for correlation.
   Regards, Redwood Security"

Review cadence and ownership:
- This playbook maintained by security-and-compliance team. Review quarterly or after any incident involving keys.
- Owners: Security Engineering (Aisha Kapoor) primary; Platform SRE (Miguel Santos) secondary; Legal/Compliance reviewer (Priyanka Rao).

Open questions / future work:
- Standardize an HSM attestation format across vendors to include firmware hashes and slot-level integrity markers.
- Create a formal schema registry for artifact manifests so evidence bundles can be machine-verified by legal tools.
- Add automated cross-tenant blast-radius visualization to the console for investigatory use.

End of playbook.
